## Jurisdiction Overview

Indonesia reads within Atlas as a Jakarta-centered large-scale archipelagic digital-governance environment, a Dukcapil-, IKD-, SPBE-, INA Digital-, and Satu Data Indonesia-linked digital-governance and interoperability environment, a Bank Indonesia-, BI-RTGS-, SKNBI-, BI-FAST-, QRIS-, and GPN-linked payment modernization and settlement-governance environment, a PDN-, public-sector ICT-, and mixed-provider cloud-linked digital continuity environment, a PANDI-, .ID Registry-, APJII-, and IIX-linked registry and domestic-exchange governance environment, an iDREN-, TEIN-, and BRIN-linked research-network and scientific-collaboration environment, a Palapa Ring-, BAKTI-, Telkom-, Telin-, and submarine-cable-linked telecommunications and inter-island connectivity environment, a PLN-linked energy-grid modernization and coordination environment, a Pelindo-, PTOS-M-, Phinnisi-, and National Logistics Ecosystem-linked maritime logistics and trade-connectivity environment, a BSSN- and Gov-CSIRT-linked cybersecurity and digital-resilience coordination environment, and an ASEAN-linked and globally integrated interoperability environment.

## Digital Governance and Identity Environment

Indonesia's digital governance and identity environment is characterized by Dukcapil systems, IKD systems, SPBE systems, INA Digital systems, Satu Data Indonesia systems, Komdigi digital-government integration systems, and public-service interoperability systems. Dukcapil and IKD carry continuity through a foundational digital identity environment linked to national digital-service integration. SPBE is the coordinated priority-application environment spanning multiple public-service domains. INA Digital is the integrated government digital-services ecosystem. Satu Data Indonesia is the national data-governance and official open-data environment across central and regional institutions.

## Financial Infrastructure and Settlement Environment

Indonesia's financial infrastructure and settlement environment is characterized by Bank Indonesia systems, BI-RTGS infrastructure, SKNBI systems, BI-FAST systems, GPN systems, QRIS systems, and QRIS Antarnegara systems. Bank Indonesia carries continuity through direct central-bank governance of wholesale and retail payment infrastructure. BI-RTGS is the real-time high-value settlement environment. SKNBI is the national clearing environment. BI-FAST is the real-time retail fast-payment infrastructure positioned as a backbone of retail payments. GPN, QRIS, and QRIS Antarnegara preserve nationally coordinated payment-gateway interoperability, standardized QR-payment infrastructure, and cross-border QR-payment linkages.

## Data Infrastructure and Digital Continuity Environment

Indonesia's data infrastructure and digital continuity environment is characterized by PDN Cikarang systems, national API backbone systems, Satu Data Indonesia systems, AWS Jakarta systems, Google Cloud Jakarta systems, Azure Indonesia Central systems, and mixed-provider cloud environments. PDN Cikarang carries continuity through large-scale national data-center infrastructure. The national API backbone is the coordinated service-exchange environment connected to SPBE integration. The package preserves a mixed-provider boundary rather than a wholly sovereign public-cloud stack.

## Internet Exchange and Registry Governance Environment

Indonesia's internet exchange and registry-governance environment is characterized by PANDI systems, .ID registry-governance systems, APJII systems, and IIX systems. PANDI carries continuity through formal .ID registry and DNS-governance administration. APJII is the institutionally documented domestic interconnection environment. IIX is the local interconnection structure intended to keep domestic traffic from transiting abroad before returning to Indonesian networks.

## Telecommunications and Inter-Island Connectivity Environment

Indonesia's telecommunications and inter-island connectivity environment is characterized by Palapa Ring systems, BAKTI BTS 4G systems, Telkom neuCentrIX systems, Telin cable systems, Bifrost cable systems, and submarine-cable landing systems. Palapa Ring carries continuity through a multi-island national fiber backbone. BAKTI BTS 4G is the nationally coordinated rural and underserved-area access expansion. Telin cable systems and Bifrost landings are international submarine-cable participation linked to Indonesian landing points.

## Research Network and Scientific Infrastructure Environment

Indonesia's research network and scientific infrastructure environment is characterized by iDREN systems, TEIN research-network connectivity, BRIN-linked HPC systems, ASEAN-Korea HPC infrastructure, and Indonesia-Korea HPC collaboration systems. iDREN carries continuity through a shared research-and-education networking environment. TEIN linkage is the formal international research-network participation environment. BRIN-linked ASEAN-Korea HPC infrastructure and Indonesia-Korea HPC collaboration are the main scientific-compute and regional capacity-building anchors.

## Energy and Industrial Coordination Environment

Indonesia's energy and industrial coordination environment is characterized by PLN grid-modernization systems, smart-grid systems, advanced forecasting systems, and inter-island transmission systems. PLN carries continuity through a nationally coordinated grid-modernization environment. Smart-grid deployment and advanced forecasting support renewable-integration and system reliability, efficiency, security, and flexibility.

## Logistics and Maritime Connectivity Environment

Indonesia's logistics and maritime connectivity environment is characterized by Pelindo PTOS-M systems, Phinnisi systems, National Logistics Ecosystem systems, and port digitization systems. Pelindo PTOS-M carries continuity through an integrated port operating platform. Phinnisi is the end-to-end vessel-service platform supporting cross-port connectivity. National Logistics Ecosystem alignment is the nationally coordinated logistics-standardization environment around export-import and domestic inter-island goods flows.

## Cybersecurity and Digital Resilience Environment

Indonesia's cybersecurity and digital resilience environment is characterized by BSSN systems and Gov-CSIRT Indonesia systems. BSSN carries continuity through standing national cyber coordination structures. Gov-CSIRT Indonesia is the named government-sector incident-response environment with authority for incident handling, mitigation, investigation, impact analysis, and post-incident recovery.

## ASEAN and Global Integration Environment

Indonesia's ASEAN and global integration environment is characterized by QRIS Antarnegara systems, TEIN connectivity, ASEAN HPC collaboration systems, Telin international submarine-cable systems, Bifrost cable systems, and Pelindo / NLE trade-connectivity systems. QRIS Antarnegara carries continuity through documented regional QR-payment interoperability. TEIN connectivity is the international research-network participation environment. Telin international cable systems and Bifrost landings are the international submarine-cable participation surface.

## Structural Constraints

The current Indonesia profile preserves mixed-provider cloud dependency structures, foreign-financed and consortium-built PDN infrastructure dependency structures, bounded IX-centrality evidence beyond PANDI/APJII systems, limited sovereign compute evidence beyond iDREN and BRIN-linked systems, cross-border payment/research/cable/cloud dependencies, archipelagic infrastructure deployment complexity, and bounded private-sector and all-sector cyber-governance visibility beyond public-sector systems.

Indonesia appears in the profile layer as a large-scale archipelagic infrastructure jurisdiction combining digital identity systems, public-service integration, central-bank-operated settlement and payment modernization, inter-island telecommunications, submarine-cable connectivity, public-sector cloud continuity, registry governance, research-network participation, maritime logistics modernization, cyber coordination, and ASEAN/global integration interfaces.

Komdigi's linkage between SPBE integration, the National Data Center, and a national API backbone signals continuity through service-exchange backbones. AWS Jakarta, Google Cloud Jakarta, and Azure Indonesia Central signal continuity through locally present hyperscale cloud-region infrastructure. The coexistence of PDN infrastructure, national service-exchange backbones, and hyperscale regional presence signals a mixed-provider continuity environment.

PANDI's role as the nationally administered .ID registry signals continuity through formal ccTLD and DNS-governance administration. APJII's IIX and MMR functions signal continuity in domestic interconnection. PLN's grid-upgrade activity signals energy-grid continuity through nationally coordinated grid modernization. Smart-grid solutions and advanced forecasting tools signal continuity in energy coordination through renewable-integration and grid-management systems. Inter-island transmission support and transmission-grid interconnection signal continuity through expanding transmission coordination across geographically distributed power infrastructure.

Pelindo's PTOS-M system signals maritime logistics continuity through an integrated port operating platform. Phinnisi's role as an end-to-end vessel-service platform supporting cross-port connectivity signals continuity across vessel-service administration. Linkage between Phinnisi and NLE objectives signals continuity through nationally coordinated logistics standardization. Kemenkeu's description of NLE as supporting export-import and domestic inter-island goods flows signals continuity across both external trade and domestic goods-flow coordination.

BSSN's coordination role and Gov-CSIRT Indonesia's government-sector mandate signal cybersecurity continuity through national cyber coordination structures. Gov-CSIRT Indonesia's authority for incident handling, mitigation, investigation, impact analysis, and post-incident recovery signals continuity through operational incident-response functions. The formal public-sector cyber-resilience mechanism signals continuity through documented cyber coordination and recovery capacity.

# Indonesia - Evidence Layer

## Strategic Position

Dukcapil states that Identitas Kependudukan Digital (IKD) is being positioned as a foundational digital identity for government services under Perpres No. 82 Tahun 2023, while Satu Data Indonesia states that it is the government data-governance policy for sharable data across central and regional institutions. INA Digital states that it exists to build an integrated government digital-services ecosystem tied to Perpres No. 82 Tahun 2023, while Komdigi states that SPBE is the main foundation of national digital government. Bank Indonesia states that BI-RTGS is the national high-value transfer infrastructure, SKNBI is the national clearing infrastructure, BI-FAST is retail-payment infrastructure intended to become the backbone of retail payments, and QRIS and GPN are national interoperability layers. Palapa Ring is a national fiber-optic network connecting 90 regencies and cities. Telin states that it operates more than 250,000 km of cable systems in the Asia-Pacific and that the Bifrost cable lands in Jakarta and Manado. The National Data Center in Cikarang is being built as strategic digital infrastructure with Tier IV-aligned standards. PANDI is the .ID registry assigned by Kominfo decree, while APJII states that IIX keeps domestic interconnection local. iDREN is a dedicated network for Indonesian research and education institutions with connectivity to TEIN. PLN is upgrading grid infrastructure with smart-grid solutions. Pelindo states that PTOS-M and Phinnisi are being deployed across port operations in support of the NLE. BSSN identifies Gov-CSIRT Indonesia as the government-sector incident-response team.

## Digital Governance and Identity Infrastructure

Dukcapil states IKD is the foundational digital ID required across government services with personal-data protection. Perpres 82/2023 provides for nine priority SPBE applications including integrated education, health, social assistance, population administration integrated with digital identity, state-finance transactions, state-administration services, a public-service portal, Satu Data Indonesia, and integrated policing services. INA Digital operates as part of PERURI to build an integrated digital-government service ecosystem. Satu Data Indonesia is the government data-governance policy intended to create high-quality data accessible and shareable across central and regional institutions grounded in Perpres No. 39 Tahun 2019. Komdigi states SPBE is the main foundation of national digital government, that roughly 27,000 applications are spread across ministries, agencies, and regions, and that the government is working to integrate them within one national architecture using the National Data Center and a national API backbone.

Sources: Ditjen Dukcapil Kemendagri — https://dukcapil.kemendagri.go.id/blog/read/pemerintah-jadikan-ikd-sebagai-identitas-digital-dasar | INA Digital — https://inadigital.go.id/ | Portal Satu Data Indonesia — https://data.go.id/about | Komdigi — https://portal.komdigi.go.id/kanal-publik/berita-kini/9952

## Financial Infrastructure and Payment Systems

Bank Indonesia states BI-RTGS is infrastructure for electronic fund transfers settled immediately per transaction on an individual basis since 17 November 2000, designed for gross settlement in real time that is final and irrevocable. BI-FAST is available 24/7, operates in real time, supports push and pull transactions, proxy address use, fraud detection, automatic customer notifications, and AML/CTF systems. SKNBI is the national clearing infrastructure for funds transfers and scheduled clearing. GPN is an ecosystem connecting electronic payment instruments offered by domestic banks. QRIS is the national QR payment standard, with one QRIS code supporting multiple payment instruments. QRIS Antarnegara interconnects Indonesia's QR standard with partner-country QR standards through central-bank-initiated cooperation with settlement through appointed cross-currency dealers in local currencies, with documented partners: PromptPay in Thailand, DuitNow in Malaysia, NETS in Singapore, and JPQR Global in Japan.

Sources: Bank Indonesia BI-RTGS — https://www.bi.go.id/id/fungsi-utama/sistem-pembayaran/nilai-besar/rtgs/default.aspx | BI-FAST — https://www.bi.go.id/en/publikasi/ruang-media/news-release/Pages/sp_2333421.aspx | QRIS Antarnegara — https://www.bi.go.id/id/fungsi-utama/sistem-pembayaran/ritel/kanal-layanan/QRIS/QRIS-Antarnegara/default.aspx

## Data Infrastructure and Digital Continuity

PDN Cikarang is designed with Uptime Tier IV standards, at least 25,000 processor cores, 200 TB of memory, 40 petabytes of storage, and 20 MVA of electricity from two separate sources. Financed through loans from the French government and commercial banks, built by the Ellipse Projects consortium. AWS Asia Pacific (Jakarta) Region has three Availability Zones. Google Cloud's Jakarta region has three cloud zones. Microsoft Azure lists Indonesia Central in Jakarta as a public-cloud region with availability-zone support. The documented environment combines PDN public-sector infrastructure, service-exchange backbones, Satu Data Indonesia open-data governance, and locally present hyperscale cloud regions — a mixed-provider continuity environment.

Sources: Itjen Komdigi — https://itjen.komdigi.go.id/publikasi/berita/21 | AWS — https://aws.amazon.com/id/local/jakarta/ | Google Cloud — https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/infrastructure/new-google-cloud-region-in-jakarta-now-open | Microsoft Learn — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/regions-list

## Internet Exchange and Registry Infrastructure

PANDI is the Indonesian top-level domain name registry (.ID) assigned by Decree No. 806 of 2014. APJII provides IIX and MMR functions: IIX unifies networks operated by ISPs so domestic traffic does not transit abroad before returning to Indonesian networks; MMR functions as a cross-connect room between servers and connectivity racks.

Sources: PANDI — https://pandi.id/en | APJII — https://apjii.or.id/

## Telecommunications and Connectivity Infrastructure

Palapa Ring is a national fiber-optic network connecting 90 regencies and cities across Indonesia, with 57 service regencies or cities and 33 interconnection regencies or cities. BAKTI program has 5,321 BTS 4G sites operational in rural and underserved areas. Telkom's neuCentrIX Banda Aceh supports digital-ecosystem needs in northern Sumatra. Telin's cable-system footprint spans more than 250,000 km across Asia-Pacific routes. Bifrost connects Singapore to the west coast of North America with landings in Jakarta and Manado, positioning Manado as Indonesia's second international gateway.

Sources: Palapa Ring — https://aptika.kominfo.go.id/2020/01/palapa-ring/ | BAKTI — https://www.komdigi.go.id/berita/siaran-pers/detail/tugas-berakhir-satgas-bakti-kominfo-5321-bts-4g-beroperasi-dan-kontrak-hbs-diakhiri | Telin — https://www.telin.net/en/carrier/telin-cable-system | Bifrost — https://www.telin.net/en/company/news/telin-expands-indonesias-digital-gateway-bifrost-cable-arrives-in-manado

## Research Network and Scientific Infrastructure

iDREN is a dedicated network infrastructure connecting research and education institutions in Indonesia, with connectivity onward to global TEIN research network, supporting cross-border e-learning, video conferencing, and research-data management. BRIN materials document ASEAN-Korea HPC infrastructure intended to strengthen regional big-data and AI capabilities, ASEAN HPC school programs, and Indonesia-Korea HPC collaboration.

Sources: iDREN — https://idren.id/about | BRIN ASEAN-Korea HPC — https://brin.go.id/en/news/127731/brin-prepares-the-launch-of-asean-korea-hpc-infrastructure-to-strengthen-regional-big-data-and-ai-capabilities

## Energy and Industrial Infrastructure

PLN is upgrading grid infrastructure to accommodate variable and decentralized generation, implementing smart-grid solutions and advanced forecasting tools to manage renewable-energy fluctuations. Smart-grid technology and inter-island transmission are being positioned as supporting infrastructure for broader clean-electricity access.

Sources: PLN grid modernization — https://web.pln.co.id/pln-jetp/grid-modernization

## Logistics and Maritime Connectivity Infrastructure

Pelindo's PTOS-M is an integrated multi-terminal port operating system for non-container cargo, integrated with customer portals, vessel-service systems, and financial-service systems. Phinnisi is an end-to-end vessel-service operating platform for cross-port connectivity and synergy, implemented across 34 ports by end of 2023. National Logistics Ecosystem (NLE) ensures smooth movement of export-import flows and domestic goods flows including inter-island flows.

Sources: Pelindo PTOS-M — https://pelindo.co.id/media/508/dua-tahun-merger-pelindo-menhub-resmikan-ptos-m | Phinnisi — https://pelindo.co.id/media/552/lampaui-target-pelindo-sukses-implementasikan-phinnisi-di-34-pelabuhan

## Cybersecurity and Digital Resilience Coordination

BSSN established Gov-CSIRT Indonesia as the government-sector CSIRT under Perpres No. 28 Tahun 2021 and BSSN Regulation No. 6 Tahun 2021. Gov-CSIRT has authority for incident handling, mitigation, investigation, impact analysis, and post-incident recovery within the government sector.

Sources: BSSN Gov-CSIRT — https://www.bssn.go.id/gov-csirt/ | Gov-CSIRT RFC 2350 — https://govcsirt.bssn.go.id/rfc-2350/

## Regional and Global Integration

QRIS Antarnegara documents real-time cross-border QR payment interoperability with Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, and Japan. iDREN connects to TEIN for international e-learning, video conferencing, and research-data management. BRIN leads ASEAN HPC school and ASEAN-Korea HPC collaboration. Telin's Bifrost connects Singapore to North America through Indonesia. Pelindo's Phinnisi and NLE frameworks cover both export-import and inter-island logistics flows.

## Constraints and Structural Limitations

PDN Cikarang is foreign-financed and consortium-built alongside AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure regional presence — a mixed-provider environment rather than a wholly sovereign hyperscale stack. PANDI and APJII document .ID registry governance and domestic exchange functions without establishing exhaustive national IX topology. iDREN and BRIN document research-network and HPC collaboration without extending to a broader sovereign compute estate. Palapa Ring, BAKTI, Phinnisi, and NLE all reflect multi-island deployment complexity. BSSN and Gov-CSIRT clearly document public-sector incident-response coordination without comparable visibility into private-sector cyber-resilience structures.
